Title: Payments we owe
Description: Fees, rent, interest, support fees, repayments or milestone payments we must pay, with amount and due date or schedule. Merge late charges into the same item.
Examples: Licensee shall pay the annual fee on or before the first day of each contract year. | Borrower shall repay all advances on the maturity date.

Title: Payments owed to us
Description: The counterparty's payment terms on our invoices. Party Counterparty, so receivables can be chased.
Examples: Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice within thirty (30) days after receipt.

Title: Rebates, fund contributions, true-ups and deposit top-ups
Description: Calculated payments tied to a period or event: volume rebates, marketing fund contributions, true-up invoices, restoring a security deposit.
Examples: Within 45 days after each quarter, pay the rebate earned for that quarter with a calculation statement.

Title: Supplier price-increase limits and notice
Description: The other side may raise what we pay only within a cap and after notice. Counterparty, Event-driven.
Examples: Provider may increase fees once per year by up to 5% on 60 days' prior written notice.

Title: Periodic operational report
Description: Recurring service-level, sales, inventory or usage reports due after each period.
Examples: Within 20 days after each calendar quarter, deliver a report of net sales and inventory on hand.

Title: Financial statements and compliance certificates
Description: Lender or investor reporting: periodic financial statements and officer-signed compliance certificates.
Examples: Within 45 days after each fiscal quarter, deliver a compliance certificate signed by the CFO.

Title: Non-renewal notice before automatic renewal
Description: Last day to stop an auto-renewing contract or service. Due date = term end minus the notice period.
Examples: Either party may give notice of non-renewal at least 90 days before the end of the then-current term.

Title: Renewal, extension or transition option window
Description: A right that lapses unless exercised by a deadline or inside a window (renewal or extension option, transition assistance request). Due date = last day; note when the window opens.
Examples: Tenant may exercise the option by notice no earlier than 12 and no later than 9 months before expiration.

Title: Renewal decision before fixed expiry
Description: A contract that ends on a date without automatic renewal: decide and sign any renewal before expiry. Created when expiry is within 12 months.
Examples: This agreement expires on its stated date and may be renewed only by a written agreement signed before then.

Title: Termination for convenience notice
Description: Notice either party must give to end the contract without cause. Event-driven.
Examples: Either party may terminate this agreement for convenience on 60 days' prior written notice.

Title: Fee-increase notice we must give
Description: Our price increase at renewal is valid only if notice is given by a deadline.
Examples: Supplier may increase fees for a renewal term by giving notice at least 60 days before that term starts.

Title: Change-of-control or assignment notice
Description: Notice due after a change of control, merger or assignment. Event-driven.
Examples: Distributor shall notify Supplier in writing within 30 days after any change of control.

Title: Audit cooperation
Description: The other side's audit right creates our duty to cooperate after their notice. Our own discretionary audit rights are not tracked.
Examples: On 30 days' notice, Customer may audit Supplier's records once per year; Supplier shall cooperate.

Title: License usage certification or true-up
Description: Periodic certification of users, seats or volumes, and payment for any excess.
Examples: Within 30 days after each anniversary, certify the peak number of named users.

Title: Compliance deliverables: certificates, attestations and plans
Description: Reports, certificates or plans due on a date or each year: SOC reports, inspection or permit certificates, continuity or security plans. The other side's delivery is Counterparty.
Examples: Processor shall deliver an updated SOC 2 Type II report by October 1 each year. | Within 60 days, deliver an updated disaster recovery plan.

Title: Restrictive covenants and pricing commitments
Description: Standing restrictions to monitor: exclusivity, non-compete, license-use limits, most-favoured pricing and the duty to extend better pricing.
Examples: Licensee shall not permit any affiliate or third party to use the software.

Title: Financial covenants and default notices
Description: Minimum liquidity or ratio covenants, and notifying a lender or counterparty of a default within a set time.
Examples: Borrower shall notify the bank within five business days after becoming aware of any default.

Title: Service-level commitment
Description: Measurable service levels (availability %, response or resolution times), ours or the other side's. Ongoing.
Examples: Provider shall maintain monthly availability of at least 99.9%.

Title: Service credits: issue or claim within the window
Description: Credits we must issue after a miss, or credits we must claim before the window closes.
Examples: To receive a service credit, Customer must submit a claim within 30 days after the end of the month.

Title: Maintain insurance and deliver certificates
Description: Keep required coverage and deliver certificates or endorsements by a date or each year. One item, dated by the certificate.
Examples: Maintain general liability insurance and deliver a certificate of insurance by January 15 each year.

Title: Confidentiality
Description: Protect the other side's confidential information during the term and any survival period. Usually Both, Ongoing.
Examples: Each party shall hold the other party's confidential information in confidence.

Title: Personal data breach notification
Description: Notify of a personal data or security breach within a set time. Event-driven.
Examples: Processor shall notify Controller of any personal data breach within 48 hours after becoming aware of it.

Title: Sub-processor notice and objection window
Description: The processor's advance notice of new sub-processors, and our window to object.
Examples: Controller may object in writing within 15 days after receiving notice of a new sub-processor.

Title: Minimum purchase or volume commitment
Description: Minimum spend or volume per period; a shortfall triggers a remedy.
Examples: Distributor shall purchase products of at least $500,000 in each contract year.

Title: Forecasts and periodic commercial reviews
Description: Rolling forecasts and scheduled pricing or business reviews.
Examples: By the 5th of each month, provide a rolling six-month forecast.

Title: Product discontinuation and last-time-buy notice
Description: The supplier's notice before discontinuing a product. Counterparty, Event-driven.
Examples: Supplier shall give at least 90 days' notice before discontinuing any product.

Title: Defect, damage or repair notice window
Description: Notice we must give within a set time after delivery or discovery, or rights are lost.
Examples: Buyer shall notify Supplier of any defect within 14 days after delivery.

Title: Post-signing deliverable
Description: A one-time commercial plan or setup task due within a set time after the effective date.
Examples: Within 90 days after the effective date, submit an initial marketing plan for approval.

Title: Key personnel continuity
Description: Named key people who may not be replaced without notice or approval.
Examples: Supplier shall not replace the named account director without Customer's prior written approval.

Title: Contacts, notice addresses and invoicing logistics
Description: Designating contacts, notice addresses, where invoices go, issuing our own routine invoices. Payment amounts and deadlines are tracked separately.
Examples: Each party shall designate a point of contact. | Invoices shall be sent to the accounts payable mailbox.

Title: Good-faith cooperation and general conduct
Description: General promises to cooperate or act in good faith, with no action, date or deliverable.
Examples: The parties shall cooperate in good faith in the performance of this agreement.

Title: Interpretive and legal boilerplate
Description: Headings, counterparts, own costs, governing law, entire agreement, severability, force majeure, survival, waivers, liability caps, termination for cause, remedies.
Examples: Headings are for convenience only. | Each party shall bear its own costs.

Title: Routine service delivery and site rules
Description: Uniforms, badges, site access, hours, permitted use, signage, service descriptions and general performance standards with no measurable level, trigger, date or deliverable.
Examples: Supplier staff shall wear uniforms and identification badges. | Provider will perform the services in a professional manner.

Title: Conditions met at signing
Description: Payments, deposits or deliverables completed at or before signing, including conditions to effectiveness of an agreement now in effect.
Examples: As a condition to effectiveness, Borrower shall pay the facility fee on the closing date.

Title: Efforts-based or third-party duties
Description: Reasonable or best efforts duties with no measurable outcome, and duties placed on affiliates, subcontractors or others who did not sign.
Examples: Reseller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to promote the products.

Title: Indemnity claim notices and defense procedures
Description: Procedural duties after a third-party claim (prompt notice, defense, cooperation); Legal decides case by case.
Examples: The indemnified party shall promptly notify the indemnifying party of any claim.

Title: Record retention and end-of-term data return
Description: Keep records for a period, or return or delete data at the end of the contract; often defined in another document.
Examples: Upon termination, Processor shall return or delete all personal data within 30 days.
